## School Finder: regional school data and map
- [Pensacola and Gulf Coast School Finder](https://greggcostin.com/schools): 274 source records, 271 school guides, 208 public guides and 63 private guides across Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa and Baldwin counties.
- [Sources and methodology](https://greggcostin.com/schools#school-data-methodology): NCES public directory 2024-25; private directory and affiliation data 2023-24; 119 Florida grades 2025-26; 46 Alabama grades 2024-25. Data compilation 2026-09-06. Page review 2026-09-08.
- [School data JSON](https://greggcostin.com/data/school-finder.json) and [CSV](https://greggcostin.com/data/school-finder.csv): Source identifiers, dated facts, original source URLs and missing values.
- [School finder questions](https://greggcostin.com/schools#school-finder-faq): Attendance boundaries, state-grade comparability, private/Christian school types, distances and corrections.
The civilian edition connects school research with local home searches. The two editions use the same corpus and retain separate page URLs. Map locations are not attendance boundaries; driving estimates are not live-traffic forecasts. Private-school affiliation is not an academic grade. State grades should not be compared across states. Counts do not establish complete current coverage, a school ranking or market exclusivity.

## Buy a Home in Pensacola, FL | The Costin Team
URL: https://greggcostin.com/buy

Buy a home in Pensacola From first showing to closing table: an Accredited Buyer's Representative on your side, a live MLS search built around your criteria, and honest answers about every property you tour. Pensacola's market rewards prepared buyers. Inventory moves in bands: the right home in a popular price range can go under contract in days, while overpriced listings sit. The difference between winning and overpaying is preparation, real comparable data, and a negotiator who does this every week. Closing day: the moment the keys become yours. Photo: Shixart1985 , CC BY 2.0 What you get with buyer representation A fiduciary on your side of the table. The listing agent works for the seller. Your agent works for you, and that difference shows up in thousands of dollars at the closing table. Certified expertise. Gregg holds the Accredited Buyer's Representative (ABR) and Real Estate Negotiation Expert (RENE) designations, advanced training most agents never complete. Comparable sales before you offer. Every offer is built from recent closed sales, not the list price. A proven vendor bench. Lenders who close on time, inspectors who find what matters, and title companies that communicate. Compensation in writing, up front. Buyer-agent compensation is negotiable and agreed before you tour a single home. In many transactions it can be covered by the seller or structured into the offer. The buying process, step by step Strategy call. Fifteen minutes on goals, timeline, and budget. Free and pressure-free. Pre-approval. A real lender commitment, not an online pre-qualification. We can introduce you to lenders who consistently close on time. Targeted search. Two or three neighborhoods that actually fit, plus live MLS alerts the moment a match hits the market. Tour and evaluate. Honest assessments of every property, including the ones you should walk away from. Offer and negotiate. Comp-based pricing, clean contingencies, and RENE-certified negotiation on repairs and terms. Inspect, appraise, close. We manage every deadline through closing day, and hand you the keys. Search live MLS listings Set up a personalized search with live alerts, or browse the map by city. The search is the same one local agents use, updated directly from the MLS. Set Up My Home Search Pensacola Gulf Breeze Pace Milton Cantonment Navarre Fort Walton Beach Destin First time buying? You are exactly who this team was built for. First-time buyers get extra time on the fundamentals: what pre-approval really means, how earnest money works, what inspections cover, and what your monthly payment actually includes. No question is too basic. I'm a First-Time Buyer Financing, in plain English Conventional: 3 to 20 percent down. The default for most repeat buyers with solid credit. FHA: 3.5 percent down with flexible credit requirements. Good for rebuilding credit profiles. VA: Zero down for eligible service members and veterans. If that is you, our military division has the deepest VA loan library on the Gulf Coast: see the VA Loan Guide . USDA: Zero down in eligible rural areas, including parts of Milton, Pace, and north Santa Rosa County. Run your own numbers with our free mortgage calculators , or compare programs in the zero-down loans guide . Buying an investment property? Escambia and Santa Rosa County offer strong rental fundamentals: steady demand, landlord-friendly law, and price points that still cash-flow. We help investors run the numbers honestly before writing a single offer. Talk Investment Strategy Frequently asked questions Do I need 20 percent down to buy in Pensacola? No. Conventional loans start at 3 to 5 percent down, FHA at 3.5 percent, and VA and USDA at zero down for eligible buyers. Twenty percent avoids mortgage insurance, but it is an option, not a requirement. A good lender will model all of them for you. How long does buying a home take? From accepted offer to keys is typically 30 to 45 days with financing, or as little as 2 weeks for cash. The search itself varies: prepared buyers in a focused price band often go under contract within 2 to 6 weeks of their first tour. Should I get pre-approved before touring homes? Yes. Pre-approval tells you your real budget, exposes credit issues while there is still time to fix them, and makes your offer credible. Sellers in Pensacola routinely pass over offers that arrive without one. What happens during the inspection period? You hire a licensed inspector, typically within 7 to 10 days of going under contract. If the report surfaces real issues, we negotiate repairs, credits, or a price adjustment, or you can walk away with your deposit while the contingency protects you. ★★★★★ 5.0 on Google and Zillow · Verified Reviews "We had an outstanding experience working with Gregg. From the very beginning, he set himself apart." - Joshua Slavens, Google review Ready to find your Pensacola home? Set up a live MLS search in two minutes, or start with a 15-minute strategy call. Either way, you will know your next step. Start Your Home Search Call or Text (850) 266-5005

## Sell Your Home in Pensacola, FL | The Costin Team
URL: https://greggcostin.com/sell

Sell your Pensacola home Pricing built on real comparable sales, marketing that reaches every serious buyer, and a certified negotiator protecting your equity from list to close. Selling is a pricing problem, a marketing problem, and a negotiation problem, in that order. Get the first one wrong and the other two cannot save you. Here is how The Costin Team handles all three. Start with the number that matters Automated estimates miss Pensacola's street-by-street differences, flood zones, and condition premiums. Get a real valuation built from actual comparable sales, or start with the instant estimate and we will refine it together. Get Your Free Home Valuation Request a Listing Consultation Pricing strategy, not a guess Gregg is a Seller Representative Specialist (SRS) , the National Association of Realtors' premier seller-representation credential. Your list price comes from a comparative market analysis of recent closed sales, active competition, and current buyer demand in your specific neighborhood. The data is shared with you openly. You will see exactly why the number is the number, and what the pricing decision means for your timeline: priced to spark competition, priced to maximize every dollar, or priced somewhere in between. How your home gets marketed Professional photography that makes buyers stop scrolling. Full MLS exposure with syndication to Zillow, Realtor.com, and hundreds of portals where buyers actually search. A dedicated single-property website for qualifying listings. See a live example: 825bayshore.greggcostin.com . Targeted social campaigns on Facebook and Instagram aimed at active buyers in your price band. Agent-to-agent outreach to the brokerages working the most buyers in your neighborhood. Negotiation and closing Offers are where listings are won or lost. As a Real Estate Negotiation Expert (RENE) , Gregg manages multiple-offer situations, inspection repair requests, and appraisal gaps with one goal: protecting your equity. You get a recommendation on every offer, with the trade-offs spelled out, and the final call is always yours. What it costs Commissions are fully negotiable and agreed in writing before your home goes live. You will also get a net-proceeds estimate up front, covering payoff, taxes, title, and costs, so the number you plan around is the number you walk away with. Selling because of a military move? If orders are driving the timeline, the decision is bigger than list price. Our military division covers the rent-versus-sell math in depth: read Rent or Sell When You PCS or compare a cash offer against listing . Frequently asked questions How long will my home take to sell in Pensacola? Correctly priced homes in Escambia and Santa Rosa County typically go under contract in 2 to 6 weeks, then 30 to 45 more days to close with a financed buyer. Overpriced homes sit, and the longer a listing sits, the weaker the offers get. Pricing right from day one is the whole game. Should I renovate before listing? Usually less than you think. Deep cleaning, paint, lighting, and curb appeal return their cost; major remodels usually do not. Before you spend a dollar, walk the house with us. We will tell you exactly which projects buyers in your price band will actually pay for. What is the best time of year to list in Pensacola? Spring and early summer bring the most buyers, including relocating families timed to school calendars and military orders. But well-priced homes sell year-round here, and lower winter inventory can mean less competition for your listing. Can I sell if I still have a mortgage? Yes. Your loan is paid off from the sale proceeds at closing, and you keep the difference. We estimate your net proceeds, after payoff, taxes, and costs, before you list so there are no surprises at the closing table. ★★★★★ 5.0 on Google and Zillow · Verified Reviews "Gregg is an outstanding, exceptional and professional agent and advisor that is in your corner." - Shannon Williamson, Google review Thinking about selling? Start with the free valuation, then a no-obligation listing consultation. You will leave with a real number and a real plan, whether you list this month or next year. Request a Listing Consultation Get My Home Value

## About Gregg Costin | The Costin Team, Pensacola
URL: https://greggcostin.com/team

The Costin Team Precision from a 20-year Air Force career. Standards set by being a client first. A promise to out-work, out-prepare, and out-negotiate for every client. Gregg Costin · Realtor, licensed in Florida and Alabama It started with a vow Gregg's path into real estate did not start with a passion for houses. It started with a promise made in frustration. Buying his very first home early in his Air Force career, he was burned by a horrible agent. The experience left a mark deep enough that he vowed to self-educate to the absolute highest level so he would never have to rely on another agent again. Over the next two decades, moving 11 times with the military, he bought and sold homes across the United States and mastered the process from the ground up. He knows firsthand what a terrible agent feels like. Which means he knows exactly what an exceptional one takes. From the Air Force to your closing table Gregg served a full United States Air Force career, starting as a prior-enlisted Staff Sergeant and retiring as a Captain. He flew as a Combat Systems Officer aboard the E-3 AWACS through multiple combat deployments, and finished his career architecting theater-wide air and missile defense plans at CENTCOM. What that means for you as a client: plans get built before pressure hits, timelines are managed to the day, checklists actually get checked, and nobody panics on the way to closing. Mission planning and transaction management are more alike than you would think. Want the full military story, and our library of 90+ military homebuying guides? It lives on our dedicated military division site: read it at PensacolaMilitaryHousing.com . Credentials and recognition Accredited Buyer's Representative (ABR) : advanced buyer-representation training in negotiation, market analysis, and fiduciary advocacy. Seller Representative Specialist (SRS) : the National Association of Realtors' premier seller-representation credential. Real Estate Negotiation Expert (RENE) : certified advanced negotiation techniques for offers, counters, and repairs. Forbes Global Properties Rookie of the Year 2025 : recognized for outstanding transactions, sales volume, and market impact. Zillow Premier Agent with a perfect 5.0 rating. Military Relocation Professional (MRP) and Florida Military Specialist (FMS) : certified expertise for military and veteran clients. Licensed in Florida and Alabama : full coverage from Perdido Key to Destin and up into coastal Alabama. The team promise When you work with The Costin Team, you work directly with Gregg from the first call to the closing table, backed by transaction coordination and marketing support so nothing slips. Around the team sits a proven bench of lenders, inspectors, and title partners who close on time and communicate. The promise is simple: to be better than anyone else you come in contact with in this market. Best-in-class service, deep market knowledge, and fierce negotiation, so you avoid the pitfalls Gregg once faced as a client himself. The brokerage The Costin Team operates under Levin Rinke Realty , headquartered at 220 W. Garden Street in downtown Pensacola. Browse the live MLS through the team's brokerage search at greggc.levinrinkerealty.com . ★★★★★ 5.0 on Google and Zillow · Verified Reviews "He provided much more than we ever expected from a realtor." - Darin Vazquez, Google review Put the team to work One conversation and you will know whether we are the right fit. ## Perdido Key Homes, Condos & Local Guide | Gregg Costin
https://greggcostin.com/neighborhoods/perdido-key
Guide reviewed 2026-09-08.

Quick answer, as of September 8, 2026 Perdido Key offers a coastal home search west of Pensacola, with Gulf beach access and nearby lagoon recreation. Compare a condo, detached home or waterfront property by its actual access rights, complete ownership costs and location. Use the property documents and exact address to confirm beach access, insurance needs and school assignment before choosing a home. The Costin Team · Local planning guide; original sources linked below. The area Compare homes Local places Costs Schools Questions FIND YOUR PART OF THE COAST One coastal search. Three different decisions. Start with how you want to use the property: living here year-round, keeping a second home or evaluating a rental. Then narrow the map and the property type. The strongest comparison puts the view, the documents and the monthly cost on the same page. Gulf beach access Research Johnson Beach and the state park, plus any access rights attached to a listing. More than one waterfront Distinguish open-Gulf views from lagoon, canal or other waterfront settings and access. Florida + Alabama Gregg is licensed in both states, so your comparison can include the Orange Beach and Gulf Shores side of the coast. For public access details, use the National Park Service: Perdido Key Area and Florida State Parks: Perdido Key . Property access rights require the property's own records. THE PROPERTY, NOT JUST THE VIEW Compare the ways to own on the coast. Use this as a showing checklist. Compare like-for-like homes and recent closed sales when assessing price; an area-wide average can combine very different properties. Property-specific research checklist. Property choice What draws buyers What to check Build the full budget Gulf-facing condo A view, beach-oriented living and shared building maintenance. Recorded beach access; association budget and reserves; inspection reports, assessments and rental rules. Loan payment + taxes + unit coverage + dues + assessment obligations. Detached home Space and control over more of the property, with individual maintenance responsibilities. Roof and systems; flood determination; elevation information where available; any association obligations. Loan payment + taxes + insurance + maintenance + any dues. Waterfront property Direct proximity to a canal, lagoon or other waterway. The water connection matters as much as the view. Survey, seawall or dock condition; recorded access or slip rights; navigable route and any applicable permits. Home costs + applicable dock, seawall, slip and waterfront maintenance. THE COSTIN TEAM PERSPECTIVE Our local perspective: make the everyday route part of the showing. Visit the beach access you would actually use, locate your grocery and school stops, and drive the approach to the property at a time you would normally travel. Park facilities and public golf access create useful alternatives to paying for an amenity you may rarely use. This is our interpretation of the published access information, not a claim that every property includes those benefits. GET TO KNOW THE EVERYDAY PLACES Put a few real places on your map. Gulf Islands National Seashore Johnson Beach Beach crossovers, picnic pavilions, restrooms and an accessible boardwalk trail make this a useful place to experience the eastern end of the island. An entrance fee applies, and the National Park Service warns that parking can fill during busy seasons. National Park Service: Perdido Key Area Bring this question: How will you reach the beach on an ordinary weekend, including parking and carrying your gear? Beach, dunes and boardwalks Perdido Key State Park The state park pairs Gulf beach access with dune-protecting boardwalks and covered picnic tables. It is a different access option from Johnson Beach, with its own entrance arrangements. Florida State Parks: Perdido Key Bring this question: Does the property include documented beach access, or will you use a public park? A mainland waterfront option Big Lagoon State Park Big Lagoon offers a boat launch connecting to the Intracoastal Waterway. Its lagoon setting gives you a different way to spend time on the water from an open-Gulf beach day. Florida State Parks: Big Lagoon experiences Bring this question: For boating, does a nearby launch work for you, or is a documented private slip essential? Gulf frontage, deeded access, condition, association costs and assessments can change the comparison. Do not assume that it does. Check the deed, survey, association documents and any recorded access agreement. What should I review before buying a Perdido Key condo? ## First Home on the Emerald Coast: Buyer Planning Guide
https://greggcostin.com/resources/first-time-home-buyer
Reviewed September 8, 2026.
Eight steps from planning to possession Review your finances. Check credit reports, income, debts and savings. Ask the lender how a new account, employment change or large transfer would affect the application. Compare lender offers. Ask which programs fit your circumstances, what remains conditional and how to compare itemized Loan Estimates and rate-lock terms. Set the full budget. Include principal and interest, taxes, homeowners and wind coverage, flood coverage where applicable, mortgage insurance, dues, assessments, maintenance and utilities. Choose a few comparison areas. Use the community guides , actual travel routes and the property types you want. School directories require a separate address-assignment check. Review representation and the offer. Understand the written agreement, compensation, comparable sales, contingencies, deposit and contract deadlines before signing. Investigate the property. Coordinate inspections, insurance, title and association documents within the contract timetable. An appraisal does not replace your condition inspection. Confirm the closing. Compare the Closing Disclosure, lender conditions, insurance start date and possession terms. Verify wire instructions through a known phone number. Set up ownership records. Retain closing and improvement records, budget for repairs, and ask the property appraiser about any exemption for which you qualify. Collect evidence for each home, not just a monthly estimate Use the ownership-cost comparison for two properties. Save the source and date for taxes, insurance, dues and assessments. Record the address and what each quote includes. A quote for another home, a listing estimate or the seller’s escrow payment can produce a misleading comparison. For a condominium, request the association budget, reserves, inspection information, assessments, coverage and use restrictions. Use the condo document checklist with your agent and lender before relying on the proposed financing. Keep the Florida and Alabama checks distinct For a Florida property, review buyer-based taxes and any homestead eligibility with the property appraiser. Ownership, qualifying permanent residence and filing dates matter; simply closing does not establish an exemption. The Florida homestead guide explains the document questions. A Gulf Shores or Orange Beach purchase needs its own Alabama property, tax, insurance and use review. Do not carry Florida exemption assumptions across the state line. Start with the coastal Alabama guide and confirm the parcel and jurisdiction. For a VA-financed purchase or PCS, the military first-purchase companion adds eligibility, entitlement and orders questions without replacing the local property checks. Prepare the first conversation Bring your move date, preferred areas, property type, monthly comfort range and the questions you want resolved. Use the lender’s secure channel for sensitive financial records. A useful next step is a shortlist of documents or properties to compare, followed by a qualified consultation about the decision you are ready to make. Sources reviewed September 8, 2026: CFPB homebuying guidance , Loan Estimate comparison and Florida buyer property-tax guidance . Program eligibility and a specific transaction require their own review. Frequently asked questions How much should I save before buying? Separate any down payment, cash closing costs, prepaids and escrow, inspections and moving costs, and the reserve you want after closing. Loan programs differ. Ask for an itemized Loan Estimate instead of treating a percentage of price as your final cash requirement. Does preapproval guarantee the loan will close? No. Ask what the lender reviewed and which conditions remain. Final approval can depend on updated income, credit, assets, appraisal, title, insurance and other property or loan conditions. Will the seller’s tax bill become my property tax bill? Not necessarily. In Florida, a change in ownership can remove the seller’s assessment limits and exemptions. A buyer-based estimate should consider the property appraiser’s value and your eligibility. The purchase price is not an automatic final assessed value or bill. Is buying always better than renting after two years? No. Compare actual lease costs, purchase cash, complete ownership expenses and possible selling costs over your expected stay and an earlier move. Future appreciation is uncertain, and debt repayment is different from monthly cash flow. What should I confirm about representation and compensation? Ask the agent to explain the brokerage relationship, services and written agreement for your transaction. Compensation is negotiable. Confirm who will pay it and how the agreement and any seller contribution affect your cash needs. Work through your property decision with Gregg Bring the property or area you are considering, your timeline and the documents you have. Gregg can help organize the local questions for your home search or sale. Discuss my next step Compare complete ownership costs VA purchase guide Seller proceeds worksheet Contact hours: 6 a.m. to midnight Central, daily.

## Navarre &amp; Navarre Beach: Homes, Costs &amp; Local Guide
https://greggcostin.com/neighborhoods/navarre
Reviewed September 8, 2026.
Choose the setting, then verify the property Begin with how you want to use the home. A mainland address, an island condo and a waterfront property can have different daily routes and ownership obligations. Compare the exact address, property documents and services instead of treating a shared Navarre name or ZIP as one uniform housing market. Use Gulf Breeze and Fort Walton Beach as additional comparison areas when they fit your destinations. For a military move, the Navarre PCS companion adds Hurlburt and VA questions. Different questions for different Navarre property choices Choice Start with Documents to confirm Mainland home Daily destinations, access to US-98, condition and maintenance Parcel jurisdiction, provider service, insurance, tax estimate and any covenants Navarre Beach condo Bridge route, beach access and building obligations Title or leasehold documents, association budget, reserves, assessments, insurance and use rules Waterfront property Actual access to the water and maintenance responsibilities Survey, access or dock rights, condition, permits and coverage as applicable Original cost research: what the county schedule actually says The Navarre Beach Utilities rate sheet publishes a July 2026 Class I water minimum of $41.09 and sewer minimum of $47.95 for the first 3,000 gallons. Their sum is $89.04 . Using the same schedule, 5,000 gallons produces $54.49 water plus $60.71 sewer, or $115.20 . Those totals are our arithmetic from an official schedule, not observed household bills. They exclude other services, fees, taxes, deposits and connection charges. Confirm the account and class with the utility, and check whether a condo’s dues already include any of these costs. The numbers do not describe every Navarre address. The county lease amendment page describes the August 2016 authorization for $250 annual fixed lease fees and a $250 cap for variable leases through an amendment process. That page is a reason to request the executed parcel documents, not proof of the current fee for a listing. Download the dated cost evidence and assumptions . No private insurance quote, executed lease, association budget or customer bill is represented as collected evidence here. Keep tax estimates and property quotes dated The Santa Rosa County Property Appraiser says final 2026 millage will not be available until October 2026. At this September 8 review, calculations using 2025 rates remain estimates. The appraiser also notes that parcel-specific MSBU charges are additional and cannot be determined from the millage table alone. Request a buyer-based tax estimate and document its value, exemption and millage assumptions. Obtain actual insurance quotes and applicable association charges. Keep one-time connection or closing expenses separate from recurring costs. Use the two-home ownership comparison to keep the inputs and missing documents visible. A route method you can repeat For mainland addresses, compare the actual approach to US-98 and your destination. For beach addresses, record the bridge segment separately. A Hurlburt trip must use the entrance authorized for your assignment and the work destination supplied by the unit. Official Hurlburt information and Florida 511 traffic conditions support that planning. Record origin, destination and authorized entrance. Record the map provider, date, departure time, direction, distance, toll assumptions and estimated time. Compare a workday outbound trip and the return trip using the same method for each home. Keep gate processing and any omitted stops explicit. Record a driven trip separately with its date and conditions. This guide publishes the method. It does not claim a timed drive, an address-specific observation or a guaranteed commute. Connect the documents to your everyday needs Use the School Finder to research nearby options, then confirm assignment and admissions with the district or school. Distance and accountability grades do not establish the right fit for a student. Verify beach access, parking, storage, utilities and any rental use through the actual property documents. Read the military Navarre and Hurlburt companion . Both editions share the same dated cost evidence; each organizes the questions around a different move. Complete your Navarre property comparison Use these checks for your own planning. Marking them complete is your record of progress, not verification of a property or a loan decision. I compared the mainland and beach location against my daily destinations. I recorded the exact route, date and assumptions for each shortlisted address. I requested the parcel tax estimate and any leasehold or association documents. I requested insurance, utility and recurring-cost information for the property. I compared financing, cash to close and reserves using actual household figures. I listed the documents or questions still needed before an offer. Mark checklist complete Download my checklist Frequently asked questions Do the Navarre Beach utility rates apply to every Navarre home? No. Confirm the provider, account and billing class for the address. The published Class I beach schedule is for single-family or individually metered multifamily service. Mainland providers and shared-meter condominium billing can differ. Is the $89.04 utility example an observed household bill? No. It is the calculated sum of the July 2026 Class I water minimum of $41.09 and sewer minimum of $47.95 for the first 3,000 gallons. Other services, fees, taxes, deposits or connection charges are excluded. Does every Navarre Beach property have a $250 annual lease fee? Do not assume so. The county describes an amendment process authorized in August 2016 for fixed fees and variable-fee caps. Obtain the actual master lease, assignment, executed amendments and current statement for the parcel. Can I rely on a fixed commute from Navarre to Hurlburt? No. Use the exact address, authorized gate, work destination and relevant departure time. Save the route method and date, and distinguish map estimates from driven observations. Traffic and gate processing vary. Are final 2026 tax rates used in this guide? No. At the September 8 review, the property appraiser page stated that 2026 final millage would not be available until October. A calculation using 2025 millage remains an estimate, and parcel-specific non-ad-valorem charges require separate review. Gregg can help organize the local questions for your home search or sale. ### What should Florida buyers budget for closing costs?
https://greggcostin.com/blog/closing-costs-florida-buyers
Reviewed: 2026-09-09
As checked September 9, 2026, Florida taxes a standard recorded mortgage at $0.35 per $100 secured or fraction thereof, according to the Department of Revenue. Your total cash to close also depends on the contract, loan, settlement charges and prepaid costs. Ask for an itemized estimate before deciding how much cash is available for the purchase.

Regulation B separately entitles you to a free copy of every appraisal developed for your application. A low number is a financing problem, not a verdict on the house.

<!-- NATIVE_CALCULATORS -->
## Mortgage and Rental Calculators
https://greggcostin.com/mortgage-calculators
Five free native tools: monthly payments, loan comparisons, extra principal, purchase cash and rental cash flow. Illustrative inputs; sources and methods reviewed 2026-09-09.
How should you use these mortgage calculators? Start with a home you could actually buy and a rate from a written lender quote. Add the property's estimated taxes, appropriate insurance and association dues. Then use the other tools to test the closing cash, the loan structure and your plans for the home. A calculator is most useful when it makes a question visible before an offer. These tools are for buyers and owners in Pensacola, Gulf Breeze, the Emerald Coast and coastal Alabama. The starting dollar amounts are invented examples. They are not average local costs, available mortgage rates or rental-income forecasts. You can change them without creating an account. What is included in the monthly payment? The estimate combines principal and interest, mortgage insurance when modeled, property taxes, homeowners or wind insurance, separate flood coverage, and HOA or condo dues. Some costs may be paid outside a lender's escrow account. Maintenance, utilities and a future special assessment still belong in your household plan. A worked example: A hypothetical $350,000 purchase with 20% down leaves a $280,000 base loan. At an illustrative fixed 6.5% for 30 years, principal and interest are $1769.79 a month. Adding $3,500 in annual taxes, $3,000 in annual homeowners insurance, $1,000 in annual flood insurance and $100 in monthly dues brings the modeled total to $2494.79 a month. Those inputs describe no listing or lender offer. Conventional monthly PMI is zero in this example because the down payment is 20%. Different terms or costs produce different results. How are conventional, FHA and VA loans handled? Conventional is the starting choice. Its PMI input is an editable annual rate applied to the original base loan. The model uses scheduled automatic termination for a borrower who remains current. Extra principal can support a request for earlier cancellation, but the calculator does not assume that request is approved. CFPB explains PMI cancellation and termination. FHA purchase estimates use HUD's upfront premium and annual MIP table for the original base loan, loan-to-value ratio and term. Annual premiums follow the original scheduled average balance and the applicable duration. The model supports standard purchases, with the fee either financed or paid at closing. It does not decide county loan-limit or borrower eligibility. HUD's current premium structure. VA remains available for eligible buyers. You can choose first or subsequent use, a confirmed funding-fee exemption, and whether to finance the fee. VA financing is subject to eligibility, entitlement, personal-occupancy requirements and lender approval. Verify the fee and exemption rules with VA. Why compare loans over your expected ownership period? A lower monthly payment can come with higher upfront costs. Compare both quotes at the same expected sale or refinance horizon, and check the remaining balance as well as the cost. Principal repayment builds equity; interest and fees do not. The comparison makes that distinction and assumes the home's value stays unchanged. Our period-cost estimate includes interest, mortgage insurance, closing expenses and the ownership costs you enter. Starting escrow and prepaids are displayed in the cash plan, rather than added again to annualized taxes and insurance. Returns on unused cash, appreciation, sale expenses and tax effects are outside this model. Use CFPB's Loan Estimate comparison guide alongside the tool. What cash do you need beyond the down payment? Plan for lender fees, discount points, other closing charges, prepaid expenses and initial escrow. Apply only credits your lender confirms are allowed. Earnest money already paid reduces what remains due at closing. A reserve for repairs or a move is money to keep available, even though it is not necessarily a closing charge. The household budget uses take-home income and the expenses you enter. Its price-at-payment result keeps tax, insurance and HOA dollar assumptions fixed. Update those costs for any different home you consider. Your lender's qualification process is separate from deciding which payment leaves room for the rest of your life. Prepare for preapproval and review Florida closing costs . How does rental cash flow differ from rental revenue? Collected rent is the starting point. A long-term rental may leave fewer utilities with the owner but still have vacancy and turnover. A furnished mid-term rental adds setup and carrying costs. Vacation rentals depend on paid nights, average stay length, booking fees, cleaning and the time the property is unavailable for rent. The rental tool subtracts operating costs to show net operating income, or NOI. It then subtracts debt service and replacement reserves to show cash flow. Cap rate is NOI divided by purchase price. Cash-on-cash return compares annual cash flow with the initial cash invested, including the reserve you enter. A positive NOI does not necessarily mean positive cash flow. The downside case lowers rent and occupancy while increasing fixed operating expenses. It is a stress test, not a prediction. Annual averages can conceal winter vacancies or large repairs, so also review a monthly operating budget and adequate cash reserves. The displayed debt-coverage ratio uses NOI divided by debt service; lenders may use different definitions and underwriting. What should Gulf Coast buyers verify for the actual property? Obtain the expected tax bill after purchase, including applicable exemptions and assessments. Request homeowners, wind and flood quotes for the address and intended use. Review association dues, reserves, pending assessments and rental restrictions. For rentals, verify the governing jurisdiction, zoning, licensing, taxes and insurance. A projection does not establish permission to rent. Compare documented operating history with the seller's projections and account for personal use. For the local cost questions, use our Florida and Alabama ownership-cost worksheet , insurance guide , Gulf Shores and Orange Beach guide , and neighborhood guides . What are the calculation methods and limits? The extra-payment analyzer offers monthly, accelerated biweekly, weekly and custom-payment controls. The accelerated options represent 26 half-payments or 52 quarter-payments per year as one extra monthly payment spread over 12 months. Custom weekly amounts also use a monthly equivalent. Annual lump sums arrive in month 12 and every 12 months after that; custom payments start in the selected month. These are monthly planning estimates. Actual payment posting and any prepayment charges depend on your loan and servicer. Confirm how your servicer applies extra principal and partial payments. Fixed-rate principal and interest uses the standard amortization formula: loan amount times the monthly rate, divided by one minus the discounted remaining-payment factor. At zero interest, it is the loan amount divided by the number of payments. The schedule caps the final payment at the remaining balance plus interest. Prices are assumed to match the original value used for loan-to-value calculations. The tool does not handle appraisal gaps, adjustable rates, interest-only loans, balloon payments, temporary buydowns, refinance rules or a recast. The estimates are not APR, a Loan Estimate, an approval, or a promise of investment performance. Ask a licensed lender to verify the specific loan and a qualified adviser to review tax or legal questions. Calculator figures stay in the page unless you choose to save them in this browser or download them. Saving is optional and local to the device. The site may record which tool is opened, but the calculator does not send your entered financial amounts in its analytics events. Read the site privacy policy.
